title: What If the Gulf Stream Stopped Flowing?

scenes.text: What if the Gulf Stream stopped? Europe wouldn't warm up. It would freeze.
The Atlantic current system behind it is weakening, and the Gulf Stream has shifted about fifty kilometers north since 1993.
In one climate model, with the current down more than eighty percent, sea ice spreads south to Scotland, Scandinavia and the Netherlands.
Edinburgh could see 164 days below freezing a year, about half the year, and 133 more than before industry.
Winter cold extremes could reach minus thirty Celsius in Scotland, and below minus forty on Norway's coast.
Winter storms strengthen and sea level rises faster on the US East Coast. Scientists call it an early estimate from one model.
